description: Known answers for the FROST dealing, share verification, signing and rotation of §7. The fixture nsec has an ODD-y pubkey deliberately: §7.4's parity rule is the only behaviour in either document that depends on key parity, so an even-y fixture would pass whichever reading of it an implementer took. Generated with @noble/curves 2.3.0's `schnorr_FROST` — RFC 9591 over the secp256k1 taproot ciphersuite §7.4 names. Every key here is a fixture and belongs to nobody.
ciphersuite: FROST(secp256k1, SHA-256) — BIP-340 / taproot variant, RFC 9591
message: The 32 bytes signed. A real signer hashes a NIP-01 serialised event to get this; the vector fixes it so the signatures below are reproducible.

parity.description: §7.4 tells the dealer to use `a_0 = n - nsec` for an odd-y key, and names a ciphersuite that already handles BIP-340 parity itself. Dealing from the RAW nsec is what this vector does, and it produces a group key whose x-only serialisation is the npub and signatures that verify under it. The dealer-side negation is therefore not required. It is also not detectable: both `nsec` and `n - nsec` serialise to the SAME x-only pubkey, so §7.5's check of `group_pub` against the user's known pubkey passes either way.

t2.description: §7.4's co-signer parameters: t = 2, index 1 the server, index 2 a device. `commitments[0]` is the group public key; `commitments[1]` is §7.4's `commitment` (a_1·G). At t = 2 there is exactly one coefficient commitment, which is why §7.4's scalar `commitment` field is sufficient here and only here.

t3.description: §7.18 permits t = 3. The dealer emits t - 1 = TWO coefficient commitments, so `commitments` has three entries and §7.4's epoch record — which carries a single `commitment` — cannot express this key set. §7.18 states the share check as `share_i·G == group_pub + commitment·i`, generalising §7.4 over the index only; that form is false at EVERY index here, while the general form holds. An implementation that reproduces `nkm_degree1_form_holds: false` has read §7.18 correctly and found it unimplementable as written. See SPEC_ISSUES.md.

rotation.description: §7.9 tier 2 over the t = 2 set: δ(x) = r·x with δ(0) = 0, so share_i ← share_i + i·r and commitment' = commitment + r·G. `a_0` is untouched, so the group key — and the user's npub — do not change, and nothing is reconstructed. A share retained from before the rotation no longer pairs with one from after it, which is the whole property revocation rests on.

stale_share_rejected.description: Index 1's PRE-rotation share paired with index 3's post-rotation share. This MUST NOT produce a signature that verifies under the npub.
